title: Hanuma informs Seetha about Rama's victory
introduction: Matali, Indra's charioteer leaves the battle-field and returns to his heaven. Then, Rama instructs Lakshmana to arrange for the installation of Vibhishana on the throne of Lanka. Lakshmana arranges to get sea-water from some monkey-chiefs and sprinkles it on Vibhishana, to install him as the King of Lanka, in the presence of the demons there. Then, Rama sends his message to Seetha through Hanuma.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे त्रयोदशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 113th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
इति प्रतिसमादिष्टो हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः |
प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां पूज्यमानो निशाचरैः
verses.iast:
iti pratisamAdiṣṭo hanUmAnmArutAtmajaḥ |
praviveśa purIṃ lañkAṃ pUjyamAno niśAcaraiḥ
verses.translation: Thus directed by Rama, Hanuma the son of wind-god, entered deeply into the City of Lanka, being respectfully received by the demons.

verses.devanagari:
प्रविश्य च पुरीं लङ्कामनुङ्ञ्प्य विभीषणम् |
ततस्तेनाभ्यनुज्ञातो हनूमान् वृक्षवाटिकाम्
संप्रविश्य यथान्यायम् सीताया विदितो हरिः |
ददर्श शशिना हीनां सातङ्कामिव रोहिणीम्
वृक्षमूले निरानन्दां राक्षसीभिः परीवृताम् |
निभृतः प्रणतः प्रह्वः सोंअभिगम्याभिवाद्य च
verses.iast:
praviśya ca purīṃ lañkāmanuñJṇpya vibhīṣaṇam |
tatastenābhyanujJṇāto hanūmān vṛkṣavāṭikām
sampraviśya yathānyāyam sītāyā vidito hariḥ |
dadarśa śaśinA hInAṃ sAtañkAmiva rohiṇIm
vṛkṣamūle nirānandāṃ rākṣasībhiḥ parīvṛtām |
nibhṛtaḥ praṇataḥ prahvaḥ soṃabhigamyAbhivAdya ca
verses.translation: That Hanuma, the monkey, known to Seetha, having entered the City of Lanka, seeking permission from Vibhishana, getting approval from him and entering Ashoka grove as per the prevailing regulation, saw at the foot of a tree, Seetha, who was bereft of freshness, looking joylessly like a frightened cow and surrounded with female-demons. Approaching her humbly by offering salutation to her in bending his head, he stood there silently.

glosses.meaning: at the foot of a tree

verses.devanagari:
दृष्ट्वा समागतं देवी हनूमन्तं महाबलम् |
तूष्णीमास्त तदा दृष्ट्वा स्मृत्वा हृष्टाभवत्तदा
verses.iast:
dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ devī hanūmantaṃ mahābalam |
tūṣṇīmāsta tadā dṛṣṭvā smṛtvā hṛṣṭābhavattadā
verses.translation: Even after seeing the mighty Hanuma who came there, Seetha kept herself silent. Then, seeing and recollecting him, she became rejoiced.

verses.devanagari:
सौम्यं तस्या मुखं दृष्ट्वा हनूमान् प्लवगोत्तमः |
रामस्य वचनं सर्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे
verses.iast:
saumyaṃ tasyā mukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā hanūmān plavagottamaḥ |
rāmasya vacanaṃ sarvamākhyātumupacakrame
verses.translation: Seeing her cool face, Hanuma the excellent monkey began to narrate the entire message of Rama.

verses.devanagari:
वैदेहि कुशली रामः ससुग्रीवः सलक्ष्मणः |
विभीषणसहायश्च हरीणां सहितो बलैः
verses.iast:
vaidehi kuśalI rAmaḥ sasugrIvaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ |
vibhīṣaṇasahāyaśca harīṇāṃ sahito balaiḥ
verses.translation: "O Seetha! Rama is well, together with Sugreeva and Lakshmana, along with Vibhishana as his supporter and collectively with the army of monkeys."

glosses.meaning: together with Sugreeva lakShmaNaH = together with Sugreeva and Lakshmana
along with vibhishana as his supporter
and collectively with the army of monkeys

verses.devanagari:
कुशलं चाह सिद्धार्थो हतशत्रुररिन्दमः |
विभीषणसहायेन रामेण हरिभिः सह
निहतो रावणो देवि लक्ष्मणस्य नयेन च वीर्यवान् |
verses.iast:
kuśalaṃ cAha siddhArtho hataśatrurarindamaḥ |
vibhIṣaṇasahAyena rAmeṇa haribhiḥ saha
nihato rAvaṇo devi lakṣmaṇasya nayena ca vīryavān |
verses.translation: "O the divine lady! Having destroyed his enemy, Rama the annihilator of his adversaries, having accomplished his object, is informing you about his welfare. Rama and Lakshmana, with the support of Vibhishana and the monkeys, killed the valiant Ravana."

verses.devanagari:
प्रियमाख्यामि ते देवि भूयश्च त्वां सभाजये
तव प्रभावाद्धर्मज्ञे महान् रामेण संयुगे |
लब्धोऽयं विजयः सीते स्वस्था भव गतज्वरा
verses.iast:
priyamākhyāmi te devi bhūyaśca tvāṃ sabhājaye
tava prabhāvāddharmajJṇe mahān rāmeṇa saṃyuge |
labdho'yaṃ vijayaḥ sīte svasthā bhava gatajvarā
verses.translation: "O the divine lady! I am telling a pleasant news and again eulogizing you. O Seetha, the knower of righteousness! Rama accomplished this great victory in the battle, because of your power. Be free from your grief and be comfortable."

verses.devanagari:
रावणश्च हतः शत्रुर्लङ्का चैव वशीकृता |
मया ह्यलब्धनिद्रेण धृतेन तव निर्जये
प्रतिज्ज़्नैषा विनिस्तीर्णा बद्ध्वा सेतुं महोदधौ |
verses.iast:
rāvaṇaśca hataḥ śatrurlaṇ^kā caiva vaśīkṛtā |
mayā hyalabdhanidreṇa dhṛtena tava nirjaye
pratijJnaiṣā vinistīrṇā baddhvā setuṃ mahodadhau |
verses.translation: "Ravana, the enemy was killed. Even the Lanka has been subdued. With a firm determination to win you back, by me who have had no sleep, a bridge has been constructed across the great ocean and this vow (of winning you back) has been fulfilled."

verses.devanagari:
संभ्रमश्च न कर्तव्यो वर्तन्त्या रावणालये
विभीषणविधेयं हि लङ्कैश्वर्यमिदं कृतम् |
verses.iast:
sambhramaśca na kartavyo vartantyā rāvaṇālaye
vibhīṣaṇavidheyaṃ hi laṇ^kaiśvaryamidaṃ kṛtam |
verses.translation: "You ought not to have any fear, living as you do in Ravana's abode. This kingdom of Lanka has now been placed indeed under the dominion ship of Vibhishana."

glosses.meaning: for having stayed in Ravana's abode
under the dominion ship of Vbhishana.

verses.devanagari:
तदाश्वसिहि विस्रब्धं स्वगृहे परिवर्तसे
अयं चाभ्येति संहृष्टस्त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकः |
verses.iast:
tadāśvasihi visrabdhaṃ svagṛhe parivartase
ayaṃ cābhyeti saṃhṛṣṭastvaddarśanasamutsukaḥ |
verses.translation: "That is why, console yourself complacently. You are staying in your own house. This Vibhishana too is coming to you with a rejoice, as he is so eager to see you."

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी सीता शशिनिभानना
प्रहर्षेणावरुद्धा सा व्यहर्तुं न शशाक ह |
verses.iast:
evamuktā tu sā devī sītā śaśinibhānanā
praharṣeṇāvaruddhā sā vyahartuṃ na śaśāka ha |
verses.translation: Hearing these words, that Seetha the divine lady, whose face resembled the moon, could not speak, tongue-tied as she was with a thrill of delight.

glosses.meaning: with her face resembling the moon

verses.devanagari:
ततोऽब्रवीद्धरिवरः सीतामप्रतिजल्पतीम्
किं त्वं चिन्तयसे देवि किं च मां नाभिभाषसे |
verses.iast:
tato'bravīddharivaraḥ sītāmapratijalpatīm
kiṃ tvaṃ cintayase devi kiṃ ca māṃ nābhibhāṣase |
verses.translation: Thereupon, Hanuma spoke to Seetha, who was not making any answer (as follows): "O divine lady! What are you reflecting upon? Why don't you speak to me?"

glosses.meaning: who was not making any answer

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता सीता धर्मपथे स्थिता
अब्रवीत्परमप्रीता बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा |
verses.iast:
evamuktā hanumatā sītā dharmapathe sthitā
abravītparamaprītā bāṣpagadgadayā girā |
verses.translation: Thus asked by Hanuma, Seetha, who was ever established in a righteous path, was very much delighted and spoke (as follows) in a voice choked with tears.

verses.devanagari:
प्रियमेतदुपश्रुत्य भर्तुर्विजयसंश्रयम्
प्रहर्षवशमापन्ना निर्वाक्यास्मि क्षणान्तरम् |
verses.iast:
priyametadupaśrutya bharturvijayasaṃśrayam
praharṣavaśamāpannā nirvākyāsmi kṣaṇāntaram |
verses.translation: "Hearing these pleasant tidings about the victory of my husband, I became speechless for a while, overpowered as I was, by extreme joy."

glosses.meaning: overpowered as I was by extreme joy.

verses.devanagari:
न हि पश्यामि सदृशं चिन्तयन्ती प्लवङ्गम
मत्प्रियाख्यानकस्येह तव प्रत्यभिनन्दनम् |
verses.iast:
na hi paśyAmi sadṛśaṃ cintayantI plavañgama
matpriyAkhyAnakasyeha tava pratyabhinandanam |
verses.translation: "O, Hanuman! I indeed do not see any appropriate thing here, which pleases you in return, to offer you, who have announced these tidings pleasant to me, even after enervating my brain."

verses.devanagari:
न च पश्यामि तत्सौम्य पृथिव्यामपि वानर
सदृशं मत्प्रियाख्याने तव दातुं भवेत्समम् |
verses.iast:
na ca paśyAmi tatsaumya pṛthivyAmapi vAnara
sadṛśaṃ matpriyAkhyAne tava dAtuṃ bhavetsamam |
verses.translation: "Nor, do I perceive anything worthy for you on this earth for you act of conveying this agreeable news to me and on bestowing which on you, happiness may come to me."

glosses.meaning: or comparable to the act of conveying this agreeable news (to me)

verses.devanagari:
हिरण्यं वा सुवर्णं वा रत्नानि विविधानि च
राज्यं वा त्रिषु लोकेषु नैतदर्हति भाषितुम् |
verses.iast:
hiraṇyaṃ vA suvarṇaṃ vA ratnAni vividhAni ca
rAjyaṃ vA triṣu lokeṣu naitadarhati bhAṣitum |
verses.translation: "Neither silver, nor gold nor even diamonds nor the sovereignty of the three worlds, can be worthy of this message."

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु वैदेह्या प्रत्युवाच प्लवङ्गमः
प्रगृहीताञ्जलिर्वाक्यं सीतायाः प्रमुखे स्थितः |
verses.iast:
evamuktastu vaidehyA pratyuvAca plavañgamaḥ
pragṛhItAñjalirvAkyaṃ sItAyAḥ pramukhe sthitaḥ |
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Seetha, Hanuma standing with his face turned towards Seetha and with his hands joined in salutation, joyfully replied as follows:

glosses.meaning: and with his hands joined in salutation

verses.devanagari:
भर्तुः प्रियहिते युक्ते भर्तुर्विजयकाङ्क्षिणि
स्निग्धमेवंविधं वाक्यं त्वमेवार्हसि भाषितुम् |
verses.iast:
bhartuḥ priyahite yukte bharturvijayakAñkṣiṇi
snigdhamevaṃvidhaṃ vAkyaṃ tvamevArhasi bhAṣitum |
verses.translation: "O faultless lady, interested in things agreeable and beneficial to husband and wishing for his victory! You alone deserve to speak such words filled with affection."

glosses.meaning: in things which are agreeable and beneficial

verses.devanagari:
तवैतद्वचनं सौम्ये सारवत्स्निग्धमेव च
रत्नौघाद्विविधाच्चापि देवराज्याद्विशिष्यते |
verses.iast:
tavaitadvacanaṃ saumye sAravatsnigdhameva ca
ratnaughAdvividhAccApi devarAjyAdviśiṣyate |
verses.translation: "O gentle lady! These words of yours, endowed with preciousness and affection, are better than various kinds of collection of diamonds or the sovereignty over the celestials."

glosses.meaning: various kinds of heaps of diamonds
or the sovereignty over the gods.

verses.devanagari:
अर्थतश्च मया प्राप्ता देवराज्यादयो गुणाः
हतशत्रुं विजयिनं रामं पश्यामि यत्स्थितम् |
verses.iast:
arthataśca mayA prAptA devarAjyAdayo guṇAḥ
hataśatruṃ vijayinaṃ rAmaṃ paśyAmi yatsthitam |
verses.translation: "I see Rama victorious and happy, he having killed the enemies and having obtained victory. That is to say, I have attained the blessing like the sovereignty over the celestials and other good qualities."

glosses.meaning: sovereignty over the celestial and other

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा मैथिली जनकात्मजा
ततः शुभतरं वाक्यमुवाच पवनात्मजम् |
verses.iast:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā maithilī janakātmajā
tataḥ śubhataraṃ vākyamuvāca pavanātmajam |
verses.translation: Hearing those words of Hanuma, Seetha the daughter of Janaka thereupon spoke the following auspicious words to Hanuma.

verses.devanagari:
अतिलक्षणसंपन्नं माधुर्यगुणभूषितम्
बुद्ध्या ह्यष्टाङ्गया युक्तं त्वमेवार्हसि भाषितुम् |
verses.iast:
atilakṣaṇasampannaṃ mādhuryaguṇabhūṣitam
buddhyā hyaṣṭāṇ^gayā yuktaṃ tvamevārhasi bhāṣitum |
verses.translation: "You alone can utter these words, endowed with exceedingly good attributes, embellished with a grace of style and filled with an intelligence, consisting of eight excellences.*"
notes: *1) Keenness to hear discourse on the Spirit 2) readiness to hear such discourses, 3) receptivity, 4) retentive power, 5) reasoning for and 6) against a proposition, 7) the faculty of comprehension and 8) realization of truth: These are the eight characteristics of good intelligence, according to Neetisara Kamandaka, often quoted by the commentators in Sanskrit: shushruShaa shravaNaM chaiva | ghruhaNaM dhaaraNaM tathaa | uuhoapehoarthavijJnaanaM | tattvajJNaanaM cha dhiiguNaaH ||

glosses.meaning: embellished with a grace of style

verses.devanagari:
श्लाघनीयोऽनिलस्य त्वं सुतः परमधार्मिकः
ब्लं शौर्यं श्रुतं सत्त्वं विक्रमो दाक्ष्यमुत्तमम् |
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः स्थैर्यं विनीतत्वं न संशयः
verses.iast:
ślāghanīyo'nilasya tvaṃ sutaḥ paramadhārmikaḥ
blaṃ śauryaṃ śrutaṃ sattvaṃ vikramo dākṣyamuttamam |
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ sthairyaṃ vinītatvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "You are a praiseworthy and supremely virtuous son of the wind-god. Numerous good qualities are there in you along (as follows, along with others): strength, valour, knowledge of scriptures, vigour, prowess, superlative skill (in action), spirit, forbearance, firmness, stability and re is no humility. There is no doubt about it."

verses.devanagari:
अथोवाच पुनः सीतामसंभ्रातो विनीतवत्
प्रगृहीताञ्जलिर्हर्षात् सीतायाः प्रमुखे स्थितः |
verses.iast:
athovāca punaḥ sītāmasambhrāto vinītavat
pragṛhītāJṇjalirharṣāt sītāyāḥ pramukhe sthitaḥ |
verses.translation: Thereafter, having joined his hands together in salutation, standing in front of Seetha in humility and free from flurry, Hanuma again spoke to Seetha (as follows):

glosses.meaning: having joined his hands together in salutation

verses.devanagari:
इमास्तु खलु राक्षस्यो यदि त्वमनुमन्यसे
हन्तुमिच्छामि ताः सर्वा याभिस्त्वं तर्जिता पुरा |
verses.iast:
imāstu khalu rākṣasyo yadi tvamanumanyase
hantumicchāmi tāḥ sarvā yābhistvaṃ tarjitā purā |
verses.translation: "If you permit me, I wish to kill of all these notorious female-demons, by whom you have been frightened earlier."

verses.devanagari:
क्लिश्यन्तीं पतिदेवां त्वामशोकवनिकां गताम्
घोररूपसमाचाराः क्रूराः क्रूरतरेक्षणाः |
इह श्रुता मया देवि राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः
असकृत्परुषैर्वाक्यैर्वदन्त्यो रावणाज्ञया |
verses.iast:
kliśyantIṃ patidevAṃ tvAmaśokavanikAṃ gatAm
ghorarUpasamAcArAḥ krUrAḥ krUratarekṣaṇAḥ |
iha śrutā mayā devi rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ
asakṛtparuṣairvākyairvadantyo rāvaṇājJṇayā |
verses.translation: "These cruel female-demons of terrific form and behavior, with still more cruel eyes, having ugly faces, were heard by me here speaking again and again harsh words to you, who are so devoted to your husband, at Ravana's command, when you were suffering hardships in the Ashoka grove, O divine lady!"

glosses.meaning: who are so devoted to your husband
at Ravana's command gataam klishyantiim = when you were getting hardships

verses.devanagari:
विकृता विकृताकाराः क्रूताः क्रूरकचेक्षणाः
इच्छामि विविधैर्घातैर्हन्तुमेताः सुदारुणाः |
राक्षस्यो दारुणकथा वरमेतं प्रयच्छ मे
verses.iast:
vikṛtā vikṛtākārāḥ krūtāḥ krūrakacekṣaṇāḥ
icchAmi vividhairghAtairhantumetAḥ sudAruṇAḥ |
rAkṣasyo dAruṇakathA varametaṃ prayaccha me
verses.translation: "I wish to kill with various kinds of strokes, these cruel, extremely rough and deformed female-demons, with distorted features and terrific hairs and eyes, talking together roughly. (Pray) grant this boon to me."

verses.devanagari:
मुष्टिभिः पाणिभिश्चैव चरणैश्चैव शोभने |
जङ्घाजानुप्रहारैश्च दन्तानां चैव पीडनैः
भक्षणैः कर्णनासानां केशानां लुञ्चनैस्तथा |
भृशं शुष्कमुखीभिश्च दारुणैर्लङ्घनैर्हतैः
विभिन्नशङ्कुग्रीवांशपार्श्वकैश्च कलेवरैः |
निपात्य हन्तुमिच्छमि तव विप्रियकारिणीः
verses.iast:
muṣṭibhiḥ pAṇibhiścaiva caraṇaiścaiva śobhane |
jaṇ^ghājānuprahāraiśca dantānāṃ caiva pīḍanaiḥ
bhakṣaṇaiḥ karṇanAsAnAṃ keśAnAṃ luñcanaistathA |
bhṛśaṃ śuṣkamukhIbhiśca dAruṇairlañghanairhataiḥ
vibhinnaśaṇ^kugrīvāṃśapārśvakaiśca kalevaraiḥ |
nipātya hantumicchami tava vipriyakāriṇīḥ
verses.translation: "I wish to kill the female-demons, who have spoken harsh words to you and wronged you, striking them down with my fists, hand-blows, long arms, blows of my shanks and knees, by causing pain to their teeth, biting off their ears and nose and pulling out their hair, making them severely dry-mouthed, tearing them off, leaping over them, encountering them and throwing down their bodies, with their burst cheeks, necks, shoulders and ribs."

glosses.meaning: (the female-demons) who have spoken harsh words to you and = wronged you
the blows of my shanks and knees
by causing pain to their teeth
biting off their ears and nose

verses.devanagari:
एवम्प्रकारैर्बहुभिर्विप्रकारैर्यशस्विनि |
घातये तीव्ररूपाभिर्याभिस्त्वं तर्जिता पुरा
verses.iast:
evamprakArairbahubhirviprakArairyaśasvini |
ghātaye tīvrarūpābhiryābhistvaṃ tarjitā purā
verses.translation: "O illustrious lady! Striking them with several blows in this way, I would destroy the female-demons of terrible form, by whom you have been threatened in the past."

glosses.meaning: the female demons of terrible form

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्ता सा हनुमता कृपणा दीनवत्सला |
हनुमन्तमुवाचेदं चिन्तयित्वा मिमृश्य च
verses.iast:
ityuktā sā hanumatā kṛpaṇā dīnavatsalā |
hanumantamuvācedaṃ cintayitvā mimṛśya ca
verses.translation: Reflecting as pondering for a while, when spoke thus by Hanuma, the compassionate Seetha, who was kind to the miserable, spoke to Hanuma as follows:

glosses.meaning: who was kind to the miserable

verses.devanagari:
राजसंश्रयवश्यानां कुर्वतीनां पराज्ञया |
विधेयानां च दासीनां कः कुप्येद्वानरोत्तम
verses.iast:
rAjasaṃśrayavaśyAnAṃ kurvatInAṃ parAGYayA |
vidheyAnAṃ ca dAsInAṃ kaḥ kupyedvAnarottama
verses.translation: "O the foremost of monkey! Who will be angry with servant-maids, who are dependent on their king's command and work in obedience to the orders of others?"

glosses.meaning: who are dependent on the command of their king
in obedience to the orders of others.

verses.devanagari:
भाग्यवैषम्य योगेन पुरा दुश्चरितेन च |
मयैतेत्प्राप्यते सर्वं स्वकृतं ह्युपभुज्यते
verses.iast:
bhAgyavaiṣamya yogena purA duścaritena ca |
mayaitetprApyate sarvaṃ svakṛtaṃ hyupabhujyate
verses.translation: "All this is reaped by me, as a consequence of my bad fortune or an account of a misdeed committed by me in the past. The fruit of one's own making is indeed experienced (in one's life)."

glosses.meaning: as a consequence of my bad fortune
or by a misdeed committed by me
the fruit of one's own making

verses.devanagari:
मैवं वद महाबाहो दैवी ह्येषा परा गतिः |
प्राप्तव्यं तु दशा योगान्मयैतदिति निश्चितम्
दासीनां रावणस्याहं मर्षयामीह दुर्बला |
verses.iast:
maivaṃ vada mahābāho daivī hyeṣā parā gatiḥ |
prAptavyaṃ tu daśA yogAnmayaitaditi niścitam
dAsInAṃ rAvaṇasyAhaṃ marṣayAmIha durbalA |
verses.translation: "O the great-armed Hanuma! Do not speak like this. This is indeed a great divine strategy. It was ordained that this type of situation is to be obtained by me, due to the application of fate. Feeble as I am in these matters, I am forgiving the servant-maids of Ravana here."

glosses.meaning: due to the application of fate

verses.devanagari:
आज्ञप्ता रावणेनैता राक्षस्यो माम् अतर्जयन्
हते तस्मिन्न कुर्युर्हि तर्जनं वानरोत्तम |
verses.iast:
AGYaptA rAvaṇenaitA rAkṣasyo mAm atarjayan
hate tasminna kuryurhi tarjanaṃ vAnarottama |
verses.translation: "O Hanuma! As commanded by Ravana the threatened me. As he is dead now, they will not do the threatening."

verses.devanagari:
अयं व्याघ्रसमीपे तु पुराणो धर्मसंहितः
ऋक्षेण गीतः श्लोको मे तं निबोध प्लवङ्गम |
verses.iast:
ayaṃ vyAghrasamIpe tu purAṇo dharmasaṃhitaḥ
ṛkṣeṇa gItaḥ śloko me taṃ nibodha plavañgama |
verses.translation: "O Hanuma! There is an old axim possessed of merit, actually uttered by a bear in the presence of a tiger. Hear it from me."

glosses.meaning: in the presence of a tiger

verses.devanagari:
न परः पापमादत्ते परेषां पापकर्मणाम्
समयो रक्षितव्यस्तु सन्तश्चारित्रभूषणाः |
verses.iast:
na paraḥ pApamAdatte pareṣAṃ pApakarmaṇAm
samayo rakṣitavyastu santaścAritrabhUṣaṇAḥ |
verses.translation: "A superior person does not take into account the sin of those who have committed an offence evil for evil must be carried out at all costs virtuous persons account good conduct as an ornament."
notes: Formerly a tiger ran in pursuit of a hunter. The latter climbed up a tree. There was bear already preached on a bough of the tree. Making to the foot of the tree, the tiger addressed the following words to the bear: "Look here, both of us are denizens of the forest. The hunter is our common enemy. Therefore, knock him down from the tree." The bear, however, replied: "Having reached my abode, the hunter has in a way sought asylum with me. I am therefore not going to hurl him down; I would be deviating from my duty if I do so." Saying so, the bear laid himself down to sleep. The tiger now turned to the hunter and said, "Push the bear down. I shall afford protection to you." The hunter thereupon pushed the sleeping bear. The bear, however, clutched at another bough and thus escaped from falling down. The tiger now addressed the following appeal to the bear: "The hunter sought to hurl you down and has thus wronged you. Therefore push him down." Though pressed by the tiger again and again, the bear refused to hurl him down and repeated the above quoted verse in support of his attitude.

glosses.meaning: have their good conduct as an ornament.

verses.devanagari:
पापानां वा शुभानां वा वधार्हाणां प्लवङ्गम
कार्यं कारुण्यमार्येण न कश्चिन्नापराध्यति |
verses.iast:
pApAnAṃ vA śubhAnAṃ vA vadhArhAṇAṃ plavañgama
kAryaṃ kAruṇyamAryeṇa na kaścinnAparAdhyati |
verses.translation: "Kindness is to be shown by a noble person either towards a sinner or to a virtuous person or even to a person who deserves death, for, there is none who never commits a wrong."

glosses.meaning: to person deserving to be killed

verses.devanagari:
लोकहिंसाविहाराणां रक्षसां कामरूपिणम्
कुर्वतामपि पापानि नैव कार्यमशोभनम् |
verses.iast:
lokahiṃsAvihArAṇAṃ rakṣasAṃ kAmarUpiṇam
kurvatAmapi pApAni naiva kAryamaśobhanam |
verses.translation: "No evil is to be done, even to those cruel persons of sinful deeds, who take pleasure to harm the life of others and continue to perpetrate their sinful acts."

glosses.meaning: even to those who do evil-deeds
in taking pleasure to harm people

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान्सीतया वाक्यकोविदः
प्रत्युवाच ततः सीतां रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम् |
verses.iast:
evamuktastu hanumAnsItayA vAkyakovidaḥ
pratyuvAca tataḥ sItAṃ rAmapatnIṃ yaśasvinIm |
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Seetha, Hanuma who was skilled in speech, then replied to the faultless Seetha, Rama's consort (as follows):

verses.devanagari:
युक्ता रामस्य भवती धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनी
प्रतिसन्दिश मां देवि गमिष्ये यत्र राघवः |
verses.iast:
yuktA rAmasya bhavatI dharmapatnI yaśasvinI
pratisandiśa mAṃ devi gamiṣye yatra rAghavaḥ |
verses.translation: "O divine lady! You are the apt wife of Rama, full of virtue. Give me a message in return. I will go to the place where Rama is."

glosses.meaning: I will go yatra = to the place where

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता वैदेही जनकात्मजा
अब्रवीद्द्रष्टुमिच्छामि भर्तारं वानरोत्तम |
verses.iast:
evamuktA hanumatA vaidehI janakAtmajA
abravIddraṣṭumicchAmi bhartAraṃ vAnarottama |
verses.translation: Thus spoken by Hanuma, that Seetha the daughter of Janaka spoke as follows: "O the foremost of monkeys! I long to see my husband."

verses.devanagari:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हनुमान्पवनात्मजः
हर्षयन्मैथिलीं वाक्यमुवाचेदं महाद्युतिः |
verses.iast:
tasyAstadvacanaṃ śrutvA hanumAnpavanAtmajaḥ
harṣayanmaithilIṃ vAkyamuvAcedaṃ mahAdyutiḥ |
verses.translation: Hearing those words of Seetha, the highly intelligent Hanuma, the son of wind-god, bringing delight to Seetha, spoke the following words:

verses.devanagari:
पूर्णचन्द्राननं रामं द्रक्ष्यस्यार्ये सलक्ष्मणम्
स्थिरमित्रं हतामित्रं शचीव त्रिदशेश्वरम् |
verses.iast:
pUrṇacandrAnanaṃ rAmaṃ drakṣyasyArye salakṣmaṇam
sthiramitraṃ hatAmitraṃ śacIva tridaśeśvaram |
verses.translation: "You shall see today, Rama whose countenance is like a full moon, whose friends (like Sugreeva and Vibhishana) are alive, whose enemies have been killed along with Lakshmana, as Shachi (the consort of Indra) would see Indra the lord of gods."

glosses.meaning: whose countenance is like a full moon
whose friends (like Sugreeva and Vibhishana) are alive

verses.devanagari:
तामेवमुक्त्वा राजन्तीं सीतां साक्षादिव श्रियम्
आजगाम महावेगो हनूमान्यत्र राघवः |
verses.iast:
tAmevamuktvA rAjantIṃ sItAṃ sAkṣAdiva śriyam
AjagAma mahAvego hanUmAnyatra rAghavaḥ |
verses.translation: Thus speaking to that Seetha, who appeared radiant before his eyes as Lakshmi the goddess of prosperity, Hanuma of great splendor, came to the place where Rama was.

glosses.meaning: before his eyes as Lakshmi the goddess of prosperity

verses.devanagari:
सपदि हरिवरस्ततो हनूमान् |
प्रतिवचनं जनकेश्वरात्मजायाः |
कथितमकथयद्यथाक्रमेण |
त्रिदशवरप्रतिमाय राघवाय
verses.iast:
sapadi harivarastato hanūmān |
prativacanaṃ janakeśvarātmajāyāḥ |
kathitamakathayadyathākrameṇa |
tridaśavarapratimāya rāghavāya
verses.translation: Then, Hanuma the excellent of monkeys speedily narrated, in order of sequence, the message given by Seetha, to Rama who was equal to Indra the chief of celestials.

glosses.meaning: by Seetha the daughter of Janaka the king
who was equal to Indra the chief of celestials.
